episode_title: Brian Chesky on Founder Mode, Product Design, and Reinventing Airbnb
text: What people call 'Founder Mode' is really about getting into the details. Traditional management advice told founders: hire great people, give them autonomy, and step back. At Airbnb, that almost killed us. When you delegate everything, you get dozens of disconnected roadmaps and bureaucratic bloat. I run a single integrated roadmap. I review every single product feature and pixel before it ships. As a leader, you need to understand both the 30,000-foot vision and the 3-foot execution detail.

episode_title: Brian Chesky on Founder Mode, Product Design, and Reinventing Airbnb
text: To build an unforgettable product, design an 11-star experience. A 5-star experience is: you knock on the door, the host opens, the room is clean. A 6-star experience is: there's a bottle of wine and a personalized note. A 7-star is: they have a surfboard ready for you. An 8-star is: an elephant meets you at the airport. A 10-star is: you arrive with 5,000 screaming fans. You can't ship the 10-star or 11-star experience, but once you imagine it, you can easily pull back and ship a 7-star experience that blows people away and creates natural viral word-of-mouth.

episode_title: Brian Chesky on Founder Mode, Product Design, and Reinventing Airbnb
topic: Product Marketing, Combining PM and PMM
text: We got rid of the traditional classic product management role and combined it with product marketing. If you build something and you can't articulate how to explain it to a customer in one sentence, you shouldn't build it in the first place. You have to start with the press release and the customer story, not with an internal Jira ticket.
